chapter: Woody Herman and life on the road
title: Bill Evans on concentration
summary: Discussing concentration, Joe recalls Bill Evans saying he flips a switch and focuses totally.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: It’s interesting you say that about concentration because that’s not necessarily a given with musicians. You’re playing along and you’re thinking about man I’ve got to get to a laundromat or I haven’t sent my rent check home, and that’s not a good thing.

You know that’s something that Bill Evans addressed pretty thoroughly in that creative process video he did years ago with his brother Harry. And it’s something that I discuss also in the book. It’s about Bill used to say I flip a switch and then all of my concentration is focused on whatever I’m doing right then and there, and nothing gets in the way. I know exactly what you’re talking about, thinking ahead about, you know, what am I going to have for dinner, did I take out the trash, I mean blah-blah-blah. If you allow it, you could be bombarded with external input of things that don’t relate to the music or the task at hand. So that’s something that musicians, you really have to train yourself for that.
